I want to address the newlyweds now.

A woman can leave at any moment.
Then I will probably go now.
Of course, there is no one left to marry here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We will start our life over.
And where will we go?
Chef, we will tear them apart today!

meanings.en: to intend, plan, get ready to
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'gathered', paired with 'собираться'.

examples.text: Ты что, уходить от меня собрался?
examples.trans: Are you planning to leave me or what?
We got ready for vacation.
Are you planning to drink alcohol?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You sit quietly in here for now.
Denis, is that you in here again?
And there is too much cinnamon here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for the sake of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Alright, Mom, I am very glad.
We have gathered here for the sake of love.
Kostik is so very glad now.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'love' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Женщина может уйти в любой момент.
examples.trans: A woman can leave at any moment.

Run after your love!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: I wanted to talk with you.
I wanted to ruin the wedding, but returned it.
I want coffee.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оединить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to unite / join', paired with 'соединять'.

examples.trans: We want to unite two loving hearts.

Put me through to Moscow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We want to unite two loving hearts.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('loving').

examples.trans: We want to unite two loving hearts.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень любящий выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very loving choice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ердце'). Common neuter noun meaning 'heart' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня чуть сердце не встало!
examples.trans: My heart nearly stopped!
We want to unite two loving hearts.
My heart hurts.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ратиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to address / turn to'.

examples.trans: I want to address the newlyweds now.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и обратиться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to address on time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Heavy work is forbidden for you right now.

examples.text: Парни, сейчас всё в ваших руках.
examples.trans: Guys, everything is in your hands right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: This is our new head chef.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'огласный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('agree').

examples.trans: Nikita, do you agree to take Ekaterina?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'брать'.

examples.text: Откуда мы взяли ключ от номера?

examples.trans: Let us go to the kitchen quickly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Папа, он пока ещё не зять.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лностью').

examples.trans: Yes, I completely agree.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get out', paired with 'выходить'.

examples.trans: This is our new head chef.

examples.text: Всю жизнь я за тебя боялась.
examples.trans: All my life I was afraid for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Chef, forgive me for the dish.

examples.trans: This is our new head chef.

examples.trans: At the wedding I will not be alone.

examples.trans: Let us hold a fair duel today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'меняться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is canceled / called off', paired with 'отмениться'.

examples.trans: The truth is canceled.

examples.text: С этого момента вся правда отменяется!
examples.trans: From this moment on, all truth is canceled!

examples.trans: Did you understand me, my friend?
